mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate directly reflects weaker labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit growth, leading to lower equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC between UNRATE and 20d SPX returns remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20d forward return when UNRATE > 8.0% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (exceeding 0.3 percentage points in a single month) signals deteriorating labor market conditions and imminent economic weakness, causing investors to sell equities and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when UNRATE rises by more than 0.3pp in a month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate and decline in industrial production indicates a dual stress on the labor market and manufacturing sector, which signals a deepening economic slowdown and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal from the joint condition (UNRATE rising and INDPRO falling) fails to materialize: the average 20d return when both conditions are met is not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the Federal Reserve's policy rate hikes increase discount rates and reduce liquidity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 20d forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals stronger residential construction and consumer confidence, which typically precedes improved corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when HOUST is above its 50th percentile, or the Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL annual growth exceeding 2.5%) prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL annual growth exceeds 2.5%, the 20d forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and rise in unemployment rate indicates a broad-based economic contraction, which triggers a sell-off in equities and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal from the joint condition (INDPRO falling and UNRATE rising) fails to materialize: the average 20d return when both conditions are met is not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects reduced manufacturing output and economic activity, which directly pressures corporate earnings and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when INDPRO is below its 50th percentile, or the Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.
